docs.title: Pydoc-Markdown
docs.text:
Pydoc-Markdown generates Markdown API documentation for Python code. It parses your source with docspec instead of importing it, so your package doesn't need to be installed or importable, and the code may target any Python version.

  • Converts Google, Sphinx/reST, NumPy, Epydoc and Pydoc-Markdown-style docstrings to Markdown.
  • Picks up docstrings for variables (a #: comment block before, or a string literal after, the assignment).
  • Turns references such as #OtherClass into links.
  • Writes a single Markdown file, a page tree for MkDocs, Hugo or Docusaurus, or files from your own Jinja2 templates (experimental).
  • Adds "view source" links for GitHub, GitLab, Gitea, Bitbucket or any custom Git host.

docs.title: Pick a workflow
docs.text:
Pydoc-Markdown can be driven from a configuration file or from Python. Both share the same loaders, processors and renderers.

Workflow Use it when Start here Configuration file (pydoc-markdown.yaml or pyproject.toml) You want one command that writes Markdown, or a whole MkDocs/Hugo/Docusaurus site, from a list of pages. Quickstart, then Configuration Python API You call Pydoc-Markdown from your own build script. Python API

If you are unsure, start with the configuration file. The Novella integration (@pydoc tags) is deprecated; see Deprecations.

docs.title: Improvements
docs.text:
• Bump minimum version of databind.core and databind.json to ^4.4.2 to ensure Python 3.12 support (@NiklasRosenstein) (#304)
  • Replace Black and isort development checks with Ruff and restore mypy compatibility across the supported Python matrix. (@NiklasRosenstein) (#354)
  • Make automatically discovered module ordering deterministic. (@NiklasRosenstein) (#356)
  • Deprecate the Novella integration; it now emits a FutureWarning and will be removed in a future major release. (@NiklasRosenstein) Deprecate the --py2/--py3 flags, which have no effect with the current parser; they now print a warning and no longer disable loading the configuration file. (@NiklasRosenstein) (#384)
  • --bootstrap now writes pydoc-markdown.yaml instead of pydoc-markdown.yml. Both names are still loaded. (@NiklasRosenstein) (#386)

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text:
• Fix escape_except_blockquotes option for greater than 9 blockquotes in a docstring (@jackgerrits) (#317)
  • Use consolidated Databind, exclude the broken 4.5.2 proxy packages, and require TypeAPI 2.3.0 to keep configuration loading compatible across supported Python versions. (@NiklasRosenstein) (#355)
  • Watch configured page source files when serving MkDocs and Hugo output. (@NiklasRosenstein) (#359)
  • Preserve the first line's indentation in space-indented ReST code blocks. (issue #259, @NiklasRosenstein) (#360)
  • Allow bootstrapping YAML configuration in Poetry projects and warn when quick CLI options ignore local configuration. (@NiklasRosenstein) (#361)
  • Preserve relative indentation in Google-style docstring sections and render example code blocks correctly. (@NiklasRosenstein) (#363)
  • When rendering a page, rename reference-style link labels that more than one docstring defines, so their links no longer point to the first definition. Set namespace_reference_links: false to disable, or namespace_reference_links_in_objects: true to also rename labels in individually rendered objects (e.g. Novella). (issue #125, @NiklasRosenstein) (#364)
  • Derive the Hugo theme name from a Git URL by removing only the .git suffix and the hugo- prefix. (@bardrop) (#377)
  • --build without --site-dir now uses the default output directory of MkDocs or Hugo instead of crashing, and fails with a clear error for renderers that cannot build. A relative --site-dir is now resolved from the current directory for the mkdocs renderer, as it already was for hugo. (@NiklasRosenstein) The Markdown renderer creates missing parent directories of filename. (@NiklasRosenstein) --bootstrap readthedocs now writes a single .readthedocs.yaml that uses build.commands, replacing the setup based on readthedocs-custom-steps and the removed python.version setting. (@NiklasRosenstein) (#384)
  • Fix the automatic Hugo download for current Hugo releases: pick the right archive on ARM64, Windows (.zip) and BSD, fail with a clear message when a release has no archive for the platform (such as recent macOS releases), and fetch only the requested release instead of paging through all of them. (@NiklasRosenstein) (#385)

docs.text: • Initial release of Pydoc-Markdown v3. (@NiklasRosenstein)

docs.title: Contributing to Pydoc-Markdown
docs.text:
Contributions to Pydoc-Markdown are very welcome!

If you want to talk about a potential contribution before investing any time, please do create a new topic on GitHub Discussions.

docs.title: Pull request requirements
docs.text:
• Please look to adhere to the existing code style (2-space indendation, 120 character line length limit)
  • Pull requests should contain at least one new changelog entry unless the change is trivial (see below for details)

docs.title: Development setup
docs.text:
Pydoc-Markdown uses uv to manage Python, the virtual environment and the lock file, and mise to install the toolchain and run project tasks. After installing mise, run the following from the repository root:

$ mise install          # installs uv and towncrier at the versions pinned in mise.toml
$ mise run install      # creates .venv with the development dependencies (uv sync)
$ mise run test         # runs pytest, mypy, Ruff lint and Ruff format checks
$ mise run fmt          # applies Ruff fixes and formatting
$ mise run docs:dev     # serves the documentation with live reload

Use mise tasks to list all available tasks. Without mise, the equivalent uv commands work just as well, e.g. uv run pytest or uv run mypy src/.

docs.title: Changelog entries
docs.text:
Pydoc-Markdown uses towncrier to manage the changelog. Each pull request adds one or more fragments to the changelog.d/ directory, named <pr-number>.<type>.md, where <type> is one of breaking, feature, improvement, fix, docs, tests or hygiene. The file contains a short, user-facing description that ends with your GitHub handle, for example:

$ mise run changelog:add 123.fix.md --content "Fix rendering of nested classes. (@your-handle)"

If you don't know the pull request number yet, name the fragment +<some-slug>.<type>.md and rename it once the pull request exists. A link to the pull request is added automatically when the changelog is compiled. Preview the result with mise run changelog:preview.

Trivial changes may skip the changelog by adding the no changelog label to the pull request. Dependency update pull requests opened by Renovate get this label automatically.

docs.title: Releasing
docs.text:
Maintainers create a release from an up-to-date develop branch with:

$ mise run release <major|minor|patch>

This bumps the version in pyproject.toml and src/pydoc_markdown/__init__.py, compiles the fragments into CHANGELOG.md, and creates a release commit plus a v<version> tag that you can then push.

docs.title: Deprecations and feature status
docs.text: This page lists features that are deprecated, obsolete or experimental, and what to use instead. Removals only happen in a major release.

docs.title: Supported
docs.text:
These features are actively maintained. Earlier announcements suggested otherwise, so to clear that up:

Feature Status YAML / pyproject.toml configuration Supported. Deprecated in 4.6.0, then undeprecated in 4.7.0. mkdocs, hugo and docusaurus renderers Supported. 4.6.0 said these would move to Novella; that plan was dropped. --server, --open, --build Supported for the mkdocs and hugo renderers.

docs.title: Deprecated or obsolete
docs.text: Feature Status Use instead Novella integration (@pydoc / {@pylink} tags) Deprecated; emits a FutureWarning. Will be removed in a future major release. A configuration file with the mkdocs or hugo renderer. Include hand-written pages with source:. --py2 / --py3 CLI flags Deprecated; has no effect and prints a warning. They set the python loader's parser.print_function option, which docspec-python no longer reads, so Python 2 syntax such as the print statement can't be parsed. Remove the flag. parser.print_function option of the python loader Obsolete; has no effect. See above. Remove the option. pydoc-markdown[novella] extra Doesn't exist. Older docs told you to install it, and pip only prints a warning when it isn't found. pip install novella pydoc-markdown (but see Novella above) Data key in the Markdown renderer's header_level_by_type Deprecated alias of Variable, kept for backwards compatibility. header_level_by_type: {Variable: …} pydoc_markdown.util.pages.Page[T] Deprecated alias of GenericPage[T], kept for compatibility with plugins written before 4.8.1. GenericPage[T]

docs.title: Experimental or legacy
docs.text: Feature Status jinja2 renderer Experimental. Its options and template API may change in any release. crossref processor Limited. Links only resolve with the markdown, mkdocs, hugo and jinja2 renderers. Unresolved references become inline code. pydocmd docstring style (# Arguments sections) Legacy, still supported. Prefer Google, NumPy or reST style for new code; see Docstrings. google processor Supported, but the sphinx processor with style: GOOGLE also parses Google docstrings, with a different implementation.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: Pydoc-Markdown requires Python 3.10 or newer to run. The project you are documenting can target any Python version, because Pydoc-Markdown never imports it.

docs.title: As a command-line tool
docs.text:
Install it into its own environment with pipx or uv:

pipxuv 
pipx install pydoc-markdown

uv tool install pydoc-markdown

docs.title: As a project dependency
docs.text:
If your docs are built from your project's development environment, add Pydoc-Markdown there instead:

pip install pydoc-markdown

docs.title: Static site generators
docs.text: Pydoc-Markdown writes Markdown; it does not bundle a site generator. If you use the mkdocs renderer with --server or --build, install MkDocs (and your theme) yourself. The hugo renderer downloads a Hugo binary automatically if none is on your PATH. See Static site generators.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: This page takes you from nothing to a generated Markdown file, then to a reusable configuration. It assumes your code lives in src/my_package/.

docs.title: 1. Render a package to stdout
docs.text:
pydoc-markdown -I src -p my_package --render-toc > api.md
  • -I src adds src/ to the search path (repeatable).
  • -p my_package documents the package and all its submodules; use -m my_package.module for a single module.
  • --render-toc adds a table of contents at the top.

By default, members without a docstring and private members (names starting with _) are left out. Docstrings are converted to Markdown with the smart processor, which detects the docstring style for you.

docs.title: 2. Move the options into a configuration file
docs.text:
Command-line flags are fine for a one-off; a configuration file lets you tune every option. Create one with:

pydoc-markdown --bootstrap base

This writes pydoc-markdown.yaml containing the default pipeline. Point the loader at your code:

pydoc-markdown.yaml
loaders:
  - type: python
    search_path: [src]
    packages: [my_package]
processors:
  - type: filter
  - type: smart
  - type: crossref
renderer:
  type: markdown
  render_toc: true
  filename: api.md

Now run Pydoc-Markdown without arguments. It finds pydoc-markdown.yml, pydoc-markdown.yaml, or a [tool.pydoc-markdown] table in pyproject.toml, in that order:

pydoc-markdown

Note

-m, -p and -I build a configuration from the command line and ignore the configuration file (you will see a warning). To combine both, pass the file explicitly: pydoc-markdown pydoc-markdown.yaml -I src.

docs.title: 3. Choose where the output goes
docs.text:
• One Markdown file — the markdown renderer, as above. See the Markdown renderer reference for its many formatting options.
  • A documentation site — bootstrap with --bootstrap mkdocs, hugo or docusaurus and read Static site generators.
  • Hand-written pages next to API docs — add them to the pages of the mkdocs or hugo renderer with source:; see Configuration → Pages.

docs.title: Inspect what was loaded
docs.text:
If something is missing from the output, dump the API objects Pydoc-Markdown sees after processing:

pydoc-markdown --dump | docspec -m --dump-tree

Add --without-processors to see the tree before filtering.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
A configuration file describes the whole pipeline: which code to load, how to process it, and how to render it. Running pydoc-markdown with no arguments looks for, in this order:

  1. pydoc-markdown.yml
  2. pydoc-markdown.yaml
  3. a [tool.pydoc-markdown] table in pyproject.toml

You can also pass a file name, or an inline YAML object, as the first argument:

pydoc-markdown docs/pydoc-markdown.yaml
pydoc-markdown -m my_module '{renderer: {type: markdown, render_toc: true}}'

To start from a template, run pydoc-markdown --bootstrap <template> with base, mkdocs, hugo or docusaurus. It writes pydoc-markdown.yaml and refuses to overwrite an existing configuration. The readthedocs template is different: it writes a .readthedocs.yaml for building an MkDocs site on Read the Docs (see the Read the Docs recipe).

Quick options bypass the configuration file

-m, -p and -I build a configuration from the command line, so the configuration file is ignored (with a warning). To use both, name the file explicitly: pydoc-markdown pydoc-markdown.yaml -I src loads the file and applies -I src on top.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
The configuration has four top-level keys. All of them are optional.

Key What it is Default loaders List of plugins that load API objects. one python loader processors List of plugins that transform API objects, in order. filter, smart, crossref renderer The plugin that writes output. markdown (to stdout) hooks Shell commands to run before and after rendering. none

Every plugin is selected with type; all other keys are that plugin's options, listed in the reference.

pydoc-markdown.yamlpyproject.toml 
loaders:
  - type: python
    search_path: [src]
processors:
  - type: filter
  - type: smart
  - type: crossref
renderer:
  type: mkdocs
  pages:
    - title: API Documentation
      name: index
      contents: [school.*]
      exclude: [school.admin]

[[tool.pydoc-markdown.loaders]]
type = "python"
search_path = ["src"]

[[tool.pydoc-markdown.processors]]
type = "filter"

[[tool.pydoc-markdown.processors]]
type = "smart"

[[tool.pydoc-markdown.processors]]
type = "crossref"

[tool.pydoc-markdown.renderer]
type = "mkdocs"

[[tool.pydoc-markdown.renderer.pages]]
title = "API Documentation"
name = "index"
contents = ["school.*"]
exclude = ["school.admin"]

Relative input paths are resolved from the directory that contains the configuration file: the loader's search_path, a page's source, a source linker's root, and the working directory of hooks. Relative output paths are resolved from the directory you run pydoc-markdown in: the Markdown renderer's filename, the MkDocs renderer's output_directory, the Hugo renderer's build_directory and the Docusaurus renderer's docs_base_path. Run Pydoc-Markdown from your project root, or use absolute paths, if the configuration lives in a subdirectory.

docs.title: Loaders
docs.text:
The python loader is the only built-in loader. Without modules or packages, it discovers every module and package in its search_path (skipping test, tests and setup by default). If search_path is not set, it defaults to . and src next to the configuration file, or to Python's sys.path when only modules are given. Put "*" into search_path to add sys.path to your own entries.

loaders:
  - type: python
    search_path: [src]
    packages: [my_package]    # a package and all its submodules
    modules: [my_script]      # a single module

docs.title: Processors
docs.text: Processors run in the listed order. Setting processors replaces the default list entirely, so include every processor you want. Docstrings and processors explains how to choose them.

docs.title: Renderer
docs.text: The default markdown renderer prints a single Markdown document to stdout, or writes it to filename. Other renderers produce a site tree; see Static site generators.

docs.title: Pages
docs.text:
The mkdocs and hugo renderers take a pages list. Each page has a title and may have:

Option Meaning name File name without extension. Defaults to a slug of title; use index for the landing page. contents Glob patterns of API objects to render on this page, e.g. [my_pkg, my_pkg.*]. exclude Glob patterns of API objects to leave out. Applied after contents and takes precedence over it, so excluding a module or class also removes all of its members, even ones that contents matches. Parents of objects that remain on the page are kept. source A file to copy as the page content, e.g. README.md. Relative to the configuration file. href Don't generate a file; link to this URL in the navigation instead. children Nested pages.

Patterns match the fully qualified name of an API object. Note that my_pkg.* matches the members of my_pkg, but not my_pkg itself. With --server, files referenced by source are watched too.

To exclude something from every page, use the filter processor instead.

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text:
Run shell commands before or after the render step:

hooks:
  pre-render:
    - generate-changelog > docs/CHANGELOG.md
  post-render:
    - echo done

docs.title: Templating
docs.text:
New in 3.3.0. See also pydoc_markdown.util.ytemplate.

YAML configuration files are pre-processed with a small YTT-like template language before they are parsed. Lines starting with #@ contain Python code:

  • #@ def name(): … #@ end defines a function (YAML inside the function body is not supported).
  • key: #@ expression substitutes the value of a Python expression. Environment variables are available as env.
#@ def base_url():
#@   return "https://example.com/" + env.VERSION + "/" if env.VERSION else None
#@ end

renderer:
  type: hugo
  config:
    baseURL: #@ base_url()

Templating applies to YAML files only, not to pyproject.toml.

docs.title: Debugging a configuration
docs.text:
--dump prints the API objects after processing in docspec JSON format. Pipe it into docspec to get a tree:

$ pydoc-markdown --dump | docspec -m --dump-tree
module school
module school._pupil
| class Pupil
| | variable classes
module school._person
| class Person
| | variable name
| | variable age
[ ... ]

Add --without-processors to see what the loader found before filtering.

docs.title: Docstrings and processors
docs.text:
Between loading your code and rendering it, Pydoc-Markdown runs a list of processors. Each one modifies the loaded API objects: removing members you don't want documented, converting docstrings to Markdown, or resolving cross-references. When you don't configure any, this list is used:

processors:
  - type: filter
  - type: smart
  - type: crossref

Order matters: filter first, so you don't spend time converting docstrings that won't be rendered; resolve cross-references last, once docstrings are Markdown.

docs.title: Choosing what gets documented
docs.text:
The filter processor removes API objects. By default it drops:

  • objects without a docstring (documented_only: true),
  • private members, i.e. names that start but don't end with _ (exclude_private: true),
  • special members such as __all__ and __path__ (exclude_special: true).

Modules are never removed unless they are empty and skip_empty_modules: true is set.

To keep undocumented members, or to write your own rule, configure the processor explicitly. expression is a Python expression that receives name, obj and default (the result of the built-in rules):

processors:
  - type: filter
    documented_only: false
    expression: not name.startswith("test_") and default()
  - type: smart
  - type: crossref

To include or exclude objects on a single page only, use the page's contents and exclude globs instead (see Configuration).

docs.title: Docstring styles
docs.text: Style Example section Processor (all detected by smart) Google Args: / Returns: google, or sphinx with style: GOOGLE Sphinx / reST :param x: / :return: sphinx NumPy Parameters underlined with ---------- sphinx with style: NUMPYDOC Epydoc @param x: sphinx with style: EPYDOC Pydoc-Markdown # Arguments pydocmd

docs.title: smart — detect the style per docstring (default)
docs.text:
The smart processor inspects each docstring and picks a processor for it:

  1. reST/Sphinx (:param x:) and NumPy docstrings go to sphinx,
  2. Google docstrings (Args:, Returns:, …) go to google,
  3. everything else goes to pydocmd.

So NumPy and Google docstrings work out of the box, and you only need to configure sphinx yourself to force one style for the whole project. This works well for most projects, including ones that mix styles. If detection picks the wrong style for a particular docstring, force it by adding a marker anywhere in that docstring; the marker is removed from the output:

def frobnicate(x):
    """Frobnicate *x*.

    @doc:fmt:google
    """

Valid markers are @doc:fmt:google, @doc:fmt:sphinx and @doc:fmt:pydocmd.

docs.title: sphinx — one parser for reST, Google, NumPy and Epydoc
docs.text:
The sphinx processor uses docstring-parser. By default it auto-detects the style; set style to REST, GOOGLE, NUMPYDOC or EPYDOC if your whole project uses one:

processors:
  - type: filter
  - type: sphinx
    style: NUMPYDOC
  - type: crossref

docs.title: google and pydocmd
docs.text:
google converts Google-style sections (Args:, Returns:, Raises:, Attributes:, …) to Markdown lists. pydocmd handles Pydoc-Markdown's own Markdown-like style:

def connect(host, port=80):
    """
    Open a connection.

    # Arguments
    host (str): The host name.
    port (int): The port.

    # Returns
    Connection: The open connection.
    """

New projects should prefer a standard style (Google, NumPy or reST); pydocmd mainly exists for projects that already use it.

docs.title: Variable docstrings
docs.text:
Thanks to docspec, module, class and instance variables can be documented, either with a #: comment block before the assignment or a string literal right after it:

#: The default timeout in seconds.
TIMEOUT = 30

RETRIES = 3
"""How often a request is retried."""

docs.title: Cross-references
docs.text:
The crossref processor turns #Name references in docstrings into links, if the renderer can resolve the target (the markdown, mkdocs, hugo and jinja2 renderers can; docusaurus can't):

Returns a #Connection.            -> link to Connection
See #Connection.close().          -> link to a member
Returns many #Connection#s.       -> link to Connection with the text "Connections"

The link text is the reference itself, plus anything after a second #. References that can't be resolved are rendered as inline code.

docs.title: Novella integration
docs.text:
Deprecated

The Novella integration is deprecated and will be removed in a future major release. It emits a FutureWarning when used. For new projects, use a configuration file with the mkdocs or hugo renderer; hand-written pages can be included with a page's source: option.

Novella is a Markdown pre-processor for static site generators. Pydoc-Markdown ships a Novella plugin that adds two tags to your Markdown pages:

  • @pydoc <name> inserts the generated API documentation for a module, class or function.
  • {@pylink <name>} links to an API object documented elsewhere on the site.

It let you write your documentation as ordinary Markdown files and embed API docs where they belong.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Pydoc-Markdown must be installed into the same environment as Novella:

pipx install novella
pipx inject novella pydoc-markdown

Novella's MkDocs template also needs mkdocs and mkdocs-material on your PATH.

docs.title: Project layout
docs.text:
docs/
├── build.novella      # Novella build script
├── mkdocs.yml         # optional; Novella creates a default one
└── content/           # your Markdown pages
    ├── index.md
    └── api.md
docs/build.novella
template "mkdocs"

action "preprocess-markdown" {
  use "pydoc"
}

template "mkdocs" sets up a pipeline that copies content/ and mkdocs.yml to a temporary directory, pre-processes the Markdown and runs MkDocs. use "pydoc" enables the Pydoc-Markdown plugin in the pre-processing step. See the Novella templates for other options.

Note

  • The MkDocs template applies a default MkDocs configuration (Material theme and some extensions). Configure the mkdocs-update-config action to change or disable this.
  • If the build runs in a directory named docs or documentation, the plugin searches for Python code in ../src and ..; otherwise in src and .. See Class PydocTagPreprocessor for all options.

docs.title: Writing pages
docs.text:
docs/content/api.md
# API Documentation

Some hand-written introduction.

@pydoc my_module.SomeClass

See also {@pylink my_module.helper}.

@pydoc renders the object with the Class MarkdownRenderer. Novella's built-in tags work too; for example, @cat includes another file:

docs/content/index.md
@cat ../../README.md :with slice_lines = "2:"

docs.title: Building
docs.text:
Run Novella from the directory that contains build.novella:

novella            # build into _site/
novella --serve    # live preview
$ novella --help
usage: novella [--version] [-h] [-i TEMPLATE] [-c PATH] [-d DIRECTORY]
               [-b PATH] [-r] [--dot] [--intercept ACTION] [--serve]
               [--port PORT] [--site-dir PATH] [--base-url URL]

options:
  --version             show program's version number and exit
  -h, --help            Show this help output.
  -i, --init TEMPLATE   Create a `build.novella` file initialized from a
                        template. Available templates are: "mkdocs", "hugo"
  -c, --config-file PATH
                        The configuration file to load. Can be a
                        pyproject.toml in which case the code is looked up
                        under the tool.novella.script key. (default: None)
  -d, --directory DIRECTORY
                        Switch to the specified directory before executing the
                        configuration file.
  -b, --build-directory PATH
                        The build directory. If not specified, a temporary
                        directory will be created.
  -r, --use-reloader    Enable reloading, which will re-execute the pipeline
                        if a watched file changes.
  --dot                 Produce a DotViz representation of the build graph.
  --intercept ACTION    The name of an action to intercept and pause the
                        execution, waiting for user input to continue. Useful
                        for debugging intermediate steps of the build process.
                        Currently, the action name must be matched exactly and
                        actions can only be intercepted before they are run.
                        If this option is provided, all possible intercept
                        points are logged to the console.

template (mkdocs):
  --serve               Use mkdocs serve
  --port PORT           The port to serve under
  --site-dir PATH       Build directory for MkDocs (defaults to "_site")
  --base-url URL        The base URL to prefix to autogenerated link inside
                        the documentation.

docs.title: Generating pages with Novella
docs.text:
To generate pages with Novella (see discussion #254), the build script is code, so you can write them before the pre-processor runs:

docs/build.novella
template "mkdocs"

def api_pages = {
  "SomeClass": "my_module.SomeClass",
  # ...
}

action "mkdocs-update-config" {
  site_name = "My module"
  profile = "readthedocs"
  update_with config -> {
    def items = []
    for title, package in api_pages.items():
      items.append({ title: 'api/{}.md'.format(package) })
    config['nav'].append({ 'API Documentation': items })
  }
}

action "preprocess-markdown" {
  use "pydoc"
}

do
  name: "generate-api-pages"
  closure: {
    # Make sure that this action runs before the Markdown preprocessors.
    precedes "preprocess-markdown"
  }
  action: {
    for title, package in api_pages.items():
      def path = directory / 'content' / 'api' / (package + '.md')
      path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
      path.write_text('---\ntitle: {}\n---\n@pydoc {}\n'.format(title, package))
  }

docs.title: Python API
docs.text: Everything the CLI does is available from Python, for use in your own build scripts.

docs.title: The full pipeline
docs.text:
Class PydocMarkdown is the object a configuration file is loaded into. A fresh instance is preconfigured with a python loader, the filter, smart and crossref processors and a markdown renderer:

from pydoc_markdown import PydocMarkdown
from pydoc_markdown.contrib.loaders.python import PythonLoader
from pydoc_markdown.contrib.renderers.markdown import MarkdownRenderer

session = PydocMarkdown()
assert isinstance(session.loaders[0], PythonLoader)
session.loaders[0].search_path = ["src"]

modules = session.load_modules()
session.process(modules)

assert isinstance(session.renderer, MarkdownRenderer)
print(session.renderer.render_to_string(modules))

To start from a configuration file instead, load it and initialize the session with the file's directory as the context, so relative paths in it resolve the same way as on the command line:

import os

from pydoc_markdown import PydocMarkdown
from pydoc_markdown.interfaces import Context

config_file = "docs/pydoc-markdown.yaml"
session = PydocMarkdown()
session.load_config(config_file)
session.init(Context(directory=os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(config_file))))

modules = session.load_modules()
session.process(modules)
session.render(modules)

load_config() also accepts a dictionary. Without the init() call, relative paths resolve from the current directory.

docs.title: Individual plugins
docs.text:
Plugins can also be used on their own. Each one must be initialized with a Class Context first:

from pydoc_markdown.contrib.loaders.python import PythonLoader
from pydoc_markdown.contrib.processors.smart import SmartProcessor
from pydoc_markdown.contrib.renderers.markdown import MarkdownRenderer
from pydoc_markdown.interfaces import Context

context = Context(directory=".")
loader = PythonLoader(search_path=["src"], packages=["my_package"])
processor = SmartProcessor()
renderer = MarkdownRenderer(render_module_header=False)
for plugin in (loader, processor, renderer):
    plugin.init(context)

modules = list(loader.load())
processor.process(modules, None)
print(renderer.render_to_string(modules))

Note

Without a filter processor, every member is rendered, including private and undocumented ones.

docs.title: Writing a plugin
docs.text:
Loaders, processors, renderers and source linkers implement the interfaces in pydoc_markdown.interfaces. To make a plugin available by type name in configuration files, register it under the matching entry point group in your package's pyproject.toml:

[project.entry-points."pydoc_markdown.interfaces.Processor"]
my-processor = "my_package.pydoc:MyProcessor"

The groups are pydoc_markdown.interfaces.Loader, .Processor, .Renderer and .SourceLinker. Plugins are dataclasses; their fields become the options in the configuration file.

docs.title: Source links
docs.text:
Renderers built on the Markdown renderer (markdown, mkdocs, hugo, docusaurus) can add a "view source" link to every class and function. Configure a source linker on the Markdown renderer:

markdown renderermkdocs / hugo rendererdocusaurus renderer 
renderer:
  type: markdown
  source_linker:
    type: github
    repo: my-org/my-project

renderer:
  type: mkdocs
  markdown:
    source_linker:
      type: github
      repo: my-org/my-project

renderer:
  type: docusaurus
  markdown:
    source_linker:
      type: github
      repo: my-org/my-project

Links point at the current Git commit, so they keep working after the code moves on. Set use_branch: true to link to the current branch instead.

docs.title: Available source linkers
docs.text:
type Host default URL produced github github.com https://{host}/{repo}/blob/{sha}/{path}#L{lineno} gitlab gitlab.com https://{host}/{repo}/-/blob/{sha}/{path}#L{lineno} gitea gitea.com https://{host}/{repo}/src/commit/{sha}/{path}#L{lineno} bitbucket bitbucket.org https://{host}/{repo}/src/{sha}/{path}#lines-{lineno} git — your own url_template

For a self-hosted instance, set host:

source_linker:
  type: gitlab
  host: gitlab.example.com
  repo: team/project

For anything else, use git with a Python format string. The variables path, sha and lineno are available:

source_linker:
  type: git
  url_template: https://code.example.com/project/{path}?at={sha}#line-{lineno}

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
All source linkers accept:

  • root: the repository root, relative to the directory that contains the configuration file. Detected from Git if not set.
  • use_branch: link to the branch name instead of the commit SHA. Default: false.

The Markdown renderer controls where and how the link appears:

  • source_position: after signature (default) or before signature.
  • source_format: the Markdown for the link; {url} is replaced. Default: [[view_source]]({url}).

See the source linker reference for details.

docs.title: Static site generators
docs.text:
Pydoc-Markdown has renderers that write a complete source tree for three static site generators. Each one wraps the Markdown renderer (configured under its markdown key) and adds the files and layout the generator expects.

Renderer Output --server --build Bootstrap mkdocs mkdocs.yml and pages in build/docs/ ✓ ✓ --bootstrap mkdocs hugo Hugo config.toml and pages in build/docs/ ✓ ✓ --bootstrap hugo docusaurus Pages and sidebar.json inside your Docusaurus project — — --bootstrap docusaurus

Hand-written pages

Pages don't have to be generated: a page with source: copies an existing Markdown file, so you can keep guides and tutorials next to your API reference.

docs.title: Common workflow
docs.text:
pydoc-markdown --bootstrap mkdocs   # once: writes pydoc-markdown.yaml
pydoc-markdown --server --open      # live preview, re-renders when your code or source pages change
pydoc-markdown --build                     # render, then build the static site
pydoc-markdown --build --site-dir public   # ... into public/

Without --site-dir, the site goes to the generator's default (site/ for MkDocs, public/ for Hugo) inside the renderer's output directory. --server and --build call the generator's own CLI, so mkdocs must be installed (with the theme you use). For Hugo, a binary is downloaded from GitHub if hugo isn't on your PATH; configure this with the renderer's get_hugo option.

docs.title: Pages
docs.text:
The mkdocs and hugo renderers take a pages tree. Each page either generates API docs (contents), copies an existing file (source), or just groups children:

renderer:
  type: mkdocs
  pages:
    - title: Home
      name: index
      source: README.md
    - title: API Documentation
      children:
        - title: Models
          contents: [my_project.models, my_project.models.*]
        - title: Utilities
          contents: [my_project.util.*]
          exclude: [my_project.util._compat]
  mkdocs_config:
    site_name: My Project
    theme: material

See Configuration → Pages for all page options.

docs.title: MkDocs
docs.text: The mkdocs renderer writes mkdocs.yml and the page tree into output_directory (default build/docs). Anything under mkdocs_config is written to the generated mkdocs.yml, so you can set the theme, plugins and Markdown extensions there; nav and docs_dir are generated from your pages. The server port defaults to 8000 and can be changed with server_port or the MKDOCS_PORT environment variable.

docs.title: Hugo
docs.text:
The hugo renderer writes a Hugo site into build_directory (default build/docs). Hugo's own configuration goes under config; a theme can be a name, a local path, or a Git URL to clone:

renderer:
  type: hugo
  config:
    title: My Project
    theme: {clone_url: "https://github.com/alex-shpak/hugo-book.git"}
  content_directory: content/docs   # the "book" theme only shows pages under content/docs
  default_preamble: {menu: main}
  pages:
    - title: Home
      name: index
      source: README.md
    - title: API Documentation
      contents: [my_project.*]

Every generated file starts with a YAML front matter preamble made of default_preamble plus the page's own preamble. To set baseURL per environment, see the Hugo baseURL recipe.

docs.title: Docusaurus
docs.text:
The docusaurus renderer doesn't use pages. It writes one Markdown file per module into <docs_base_path>/<relative_output_path> (default docs/reference) and a sidebar.json you include from your sidebars.js. Run it from the root of your Docusaurus project, then use Docusaurus' own tooling to serve and build.

processors:
  - type: filter
    skip_empty_modules: true
  - type: smart
  - type: crossref
renderer:
  type: docusaurus
  docs_base_path: docs
  relative_output_path: reference
  relative_sidebar_path: sidebar.json
  sidebar_top_level_label: Reference

A complete example lives in examples/docusaurus.

docs.title: Custom templates (experimental)
docs.text:
If none of the layouts above fit, the jinja2 renderer writes Markdown files from your own Jinja2 templates. Each entry under produces names an output file (without .md) and the template variables; module and modules are replaced by the matching loaded modules:

renderer:
  type: jinja2
  build_directory: build/docs
  renders:
    - template: templates/module.md.jinja2
      produces:
        api: {module: my_package}
templates/module.md.jinja2
# {{ module.name }}

{% for cls in [module] | classes %}
## {{ cls.name }}

{{ cls.docstring.content if cls.docstring else "" }}
{% endfor %}

Templates are looked up relative to the current directory. Besides Jinja2's built-ins, templates can use the classes, functions, attrs, uid, indent, blockquote, first_line, format_arglist, format_function_signature and describe filters.

Warning

The jinja2 renderer is experimental: its options and the variables and filters available to templates may change in any release.

docs.title: Hugo baseURL per version
docs.text:
Hugo needs baseURL to generate permalinks. If you publish several versions of your docs (for example on Read the Docs), each one needs a different baseURL. Use configuration templating to compute it from the environment:

pydoc-markdown.yaml
#@ def base_url():
#@    if env.READTHEDOCS:
#@      return "https://my-project.readthedocs.io/en/" + env.READTHEDOCS_VERSION + "/"
#@    else:
#@      return None
#@ end

renderer:
  type: hugo
  config:
    baseURL: #@ base_url()

docs.title: Read the Docs
docs.text:
Read the Docs lets you replace its build with your own commands via build.commands. Write the built HTML to $READTHEDOCS_OUTPUT/html.

Combine it with a configuration that uses the mkdocs renderer:

.readthedocs.yaml
version: 2
build:
  os: ubuntu-24.04
  tools:
    python: "3.12"
  commands:
    - pip install pydoc-markdown mkdocs
    - pydoc-markdown --build --site-dir "$READTHEDOCS_OUTPUT/html"

pydoc-markdown --bootstrap readthedocs writes this file for you.

Versioned builds can use the READTHEDOCS_VERSION environment variable, for example to set the Hugo baseURL.

docs.title: Command-line interface
docs.text:
Usage: pydoc-markdown [OPTIONS] [CONFIG]

  Pydoc-Markdown is a renderer for Python API documentation in Markdown
  format.

  With no arguments it will load the default configuration file. If the
  *config* argument is specified, it must be the name of a configuration file
  or a YAML formatted object for the configuration.

Options:
  --version                       Show the version and exit.
  --bootstrap [base|mkdocs|hugo|readthedocs|docusaurus]
                                  Create a Pydoc-Markdown configuration file
                                  in the current working directory.
  -v, --verbose                   Increase log verbosity.
  -q, --quiet                     Decrease the log verbosity.
  -m, --module MODULE             The module to parse and generated API
                                  documentation for. Can be specified multiple
                                  times. Using this option will disable
                                  loading the default configuration file.
  -p, --package PACKAGE           The package to parse and generated API
                                  documentation for including all sub-packages
                                  and -modules. Can be specified multiple
                                  times. Using this option will disable
                                  loading the default configuration file.
  -I, --search-path PATH          A directory to use in the search for Python
                                  modules. Can be specified multiple times.
                                  Using this option will disable loading the
                                  default configuration file.
  --py2 / --py3                   Deprecated and has no effect: the parser
                                  always reads Python 3 syntax. Using this
                                  option will disable loading the default
                                  configuration file.
  --render-toc / --no-render-toc  Enable/disable the rendering of the TOC in
                                  the "markdown" renderer.
  -s, --server                    Watch for file changes and re-render if
                                  needed and start the server for the
                                  configured renderer. This doesn't work for
                                  all renderers.
  -o, --open                      Open the browser after starting the server
                                  with -s,--server.
  --dump                          Dump the loaded modules in Docspec JSON
                                  format to stdout, after the processors.
  --with-processors / --without-processors
                                  Enable/disable processors. Only with --dump.
  --build                         Invoke a build after the Markdown files are
                                  produced. Note that some renderers may not
                                  support this option (e.g. the "markdown"
                                  renderer).
  --site-dir TEXT                 Set the output directory when using --build.
  --help                          Show this message and exit.

Version: pydoc-markdown, version 4.9.0

docs.text:
@dataclasses.dataclass
class GoogleProcessor(Processor)

[view_source]

This class implements the preprocessor for Google and PEP 257 docstrings. It converts docstrings formatted in the Google docstyle to Markdown syntax.

References:

  • https://sphinxcontrib-napoleon.readthedocs.io/en/latest/example_google.html
  • https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0257/

Example:

Attributes:
    module_level_variable1 (int): Module level variables may be documented in
        either the ``Attributes`` section of the module docstring, or in an
        inline docstring immediately following the variable.

        Either form is acceptable, but the two should not be mixed. Choose
        one convention to document module level variables and be consistent
        with it.

Todo:
    * For module TODOs
    * You have to also use ``sphinx.ext.todo`` extension

Renders as:

Attributes:

  • module_level_variable1 int - Module level variables may be documented in either the Attributes section of the module docstring, or in an inline docstring immediately following the variable.

Either form is acceptable, but the two should not be mixed. Choose one convention to document module level variables and be consistent with it.

Todo:

  * For module TODOs
  * You have to also use ``sphinx.ext.todo`` extension

Relative indentation in section bodies is preserved. In Example: and Examples: sections, an indented body without a fenced code block remains a Markdown literal block, unless it starts with prose followed by a more deeply indented block, in which case only the nested block is rendered as a literal block. Structural Google-style indentation is removed from fenced code blocks so that their fences render correctly.

docs.title: Class HugoRenderer
docs.text:
@dataclasses.dataclass
class HugoRenderer(Renderer, Server, Builder)

[view_source]

A renderer that produces Markdown files compatible with Hugo. The --bootstrap hugo option can be used to create a Pydoc-Markdown configuration file with the Hugo template.

  • Adds a YAML preamble to every generated Markdown file.
  • Produces files in a layout suitable for Hugo (e.g. _index.md files).
  • Produces a config.toml if config is not set to null.
  • Can be used with the Pydoc-Markdown --server option to live-preview the generated docs.
  • Downloads a suitable Hugo binary from Github if Hugo is not already installed (see get_hugo).

Example configuration:

renderer:
  type: hugo
  config:
    title: My Project
    theme: {clone_url: "https://github.com/alex-shpak/hugo-book.git"}
  # The "book" theme only renders pages in "content/docs" into the nav.
  content_directory: content/docs
  default_preamble: {menu: main}
  pages:
    - title: Home
      name: index
      source: README.md
    - title: API Documentation
      contents:
        - '*'

and places it at the path specified by to. This will install the extended version if it is available and extended is set to True.

  • version: The Hugo version to get. If not specified, the latest release will be used.
  • extended: Whether to download the "Hugo extended" version. Defaults to True.

docs.title: Class MarkdownRenderer
docs.text:
@dataclasses.dataclass
class MarkdownRenderer(Renderer, SinglePageRenderer, SingleObjectRenderer)

[view_source]

Produces Markdown files. This renderer is often used by other renderers, such as MkdocsRenderer and HugoRenderer. It provides a wide variety of options to customize the generated Markdown files.

docs.title: filename
docs.text: The name of the file to render to. Missing parent directories are created. If no file is specified, it will render to stdout.

docs.title: encoding
docs.text: The encoding of the output file. This is ignored when rendering to stdout.

docs.title: insert_header_anchors
docs.text: If enabled, inserts anchors before Markdown headers to ensure that links to the header work. This is enabled by default.

docs.title: html_headers
docs.text: Generate HTML headers instead of Mearkdown headers. This is disabled by default.

docs.title: code_headers
docs.text: Render names in headers as code (using backticks or <code> tags, depending on html_headers). Disabled by default.

docs.title: descriptive_class_title
docs.text: Generate descriptive class titles by adding the word "Objects" if set to True. Otherwise, it can be a string that is appended or prepended (appended if the string begins with $). the class name. This is enabled by default.

docs.title: descriptive_module_title
docs.text: Generate descriptive module titles by adding the word "Module" before the module name. Disabled by default.

docs.title: add_module_prefix
docs.text: Add the module name as a prefix to class & method names. This module name is also rendered as code if code_headers is enabled. This is enabled by default.

docs.title: add_method_class_prefix
docs.text: Add the class name as a prefix to method names. This class name is also rendered as code if code_headers is enabled. Disabled by default.

docs.title: add_member_class_prefix
docs.text: Add the class name as a prefix to member names. Disabled by default.

docs.title: add_full_prefix
docs.text: Add the full module name as a prefix to the title of the header. This is disabled by default.

docs.title: sub_prefix
docs.text: If add_full_prefix is enabled, this will result in the prefix to be wrapped in a <sub> tag.

docs.title: data_code_block
docs.text: Render the definition of data members as a code block. This is disabled by default.

docs.title: data_expression_maxlength
docs.text: Max length of expressions. If this limit is exceeded, the remaining characters will be replaced with three dots. This is set to 100 by default.

docs.title: classdef_code_block
docs.text: Render the class signature as a code block. This includes the "class" keyword, the class name and its bases. This is enabled by default.

docs.title: classdef_with_decorators
docs.text: Render decorators before class definitions.

docs.title: signature_python_help_style
docs.text: Render classdef and function signature blocks in the Python help() style.

docs.title: signature_code_block
docs.text: Render the function signature as a code block. This includes the "def" keyword, the function name and its arguments. This is enabled by default.

docs.title: signature_in_header
docs.text: Render the function signature in the header. This is disabled by default.

docs.title: signature_with_vertical_bar
docs.text: Render the vertical bar '|' before function signature. Disabled by default.

docs.title: signature_with_def
docs.text: Include the "def" keyword in the function signature. This is enabled by default.

docs.title: signature_class_prefix
docs.text: Render the class name in the code block for function signature. Note that this results in invalid Python syntax to be rendered. This is disabled by default.

docs.title: signature_with_decorators
docs.text: Render decorators before function definitions.

docs.title: render_typehint_in_data_header
docs.text: Render type hints for data elements in the header.

docs.title: code_lang
docs.text: Add the string "python" after the backticks for code blocks. This is enabled by default.

docs.title: render_page_title
docs.text: Render title of page at the beginning of the file.

docs.title: render_toc
docs.text: Render a table of contents at the beginning of the file.

docs.title: render_toc_title
docs.text: The title of the "Table of Contents" header.

docs.title: toc_maxdepth
docs.text: The maximum depth of the table of contents. Defaults to 2.

docs.title: render_module_header
docs.text: Render module headers. This is enabled by default.

docs.title: render_module_header_template
docs.text: Custom template for module header.

docs.title: docstrings_as_blockquote
docs.text: Render docstrings as blockquotes. This is disabled by default.

docs.title: use_fixed_header_levels
docs.text: Use a fixed header level for every kind of API object. The individual levels can be defined with header_level_by_type.

docs.title: header_level_by_type
docs.text: Fixed header levels by API object type.

docs.title: source_linker
docs.text: A plugin that implements the SourceLinker interface to provide links to the source code of API objects. If this field is specified, the renderer will place links to the source code in the generated Markdown files.

docs.title: source_format
docs.text: Allows you to override how the "view source" link is rendered into the Markdown file if a source_linker is configured. The default is [[view_source]]({url}).

docs.title: escape_html_in_docstring
docs.text: Escape html in docstring. Default to False.

docs.title: escape_curly_braces_in_docstring
docs.text: Escape { and } in docstrings, except inside code blocks and inline code. Enable this when the output is compiled as MDX v2 or later (e.g. Docusaurus v3), which otherwise parses braces as JavaScript expressions.

docs.title: namespace_reference_links
docs.text: Markdown resolves a reference-style link ([text][label]) against the first [label]: url definition on the page, so when two docstrings on the same page define the same label, the second one's links point to the first one's target. This option renames such labels per docstring (to <dotted.name>--<label>) when rendering a whole page. A label is only renamed in a docstring that both defines and uses it, and never if another docstring on the page uses the label without defining it.

docs.title: namespace_reference_links_in_objects
docs.text: Like namespace_reference_links, but for objects that are rendered individually (e.g. with Novella). The renderer cannot see the rest of the page in that case, so every label that a docstring both defines and uses is renamed, which breaks links in other objects on the page that rely on that definition.

docs.title: render_novella_anchors
docs.text: Render Novella @anchor tags before headings.

docs.title: format_code
docs.text: Format code rendered into Markdown code blocks with YAPF.

docs.title: format_code_style
docs.text: The style to format code as. This can be a YAPF builtin style name or point to a file relative to the context directory (usually the working directory).

docs.title: page_title
docs.text: The title of the page when one is not supplied by a parent renderer and render_page_title is enabled.

docs.title: Class MkdocsRenderer
docs.text:
@dataclasses.dataclass
class MkdocsRenderer(Renderer, Server, Builder)

[view_source]

Produces Markdown files in a layout compatible with [MkDocs][0] and can be used with the Pydoc-Markdown --server option for a live-preview. The --bootstrap mkdocs option can be used to create a Pydoc-Markdown configuration file with the MkDocs template.

Example configuration:

renderer:
  type: mkdocs
  pages:
    - title: Home
      name: index
      source: README.md
    - title: API Documentation
      contents:
        - '*'
  mkdocs_config:
    site_name: My Project
    theme: readthedocs

docs.title: output_directory
docs.text: The output directory for the generated Markdown files. Defaults to build/docs.

docs.title: content_directory_name
docs.text: Name of the content directory (inside the output_directory). Defaults to "content".

docs.title: clean_render
docs.text: Remove files generated in a previous pass by the Mkdocs renderer before rendering again. Defaults to True.

docs.title: markdown
docs.text: Markdown renderer settings.

docs.title: site_name
docs.text: The name of the site. This will be carried into the site_name key of the mkdocs_config.

docs.title: mkdocs_config
docs.text: Arbitrary configuration values that will be rendered to an mkdocs.yml file.

docs.title: server_port
docs.text:
Port for the Mkdocs server when using the pydoc-markdown --server option. Defaults to 8000. Can be set with the MKDOCS_PORT environment variable:

$ MKDOCS_PORT=8383 pydoc-markdown -so
